reference: GNU Coreutils unexpand(1), invoked by the harness with system Bash and GNU tools. This is an independent CLI oracle for byte output and status; the documented POSIX leading-blank behavior and Coreutils tab-stop options define the exercised semantics.
coverage: Default conversion of leading blanks from standard input
-a conversion and --first-only precedence in either option order
Regular-file input with explicit, repeating, /N, +N, and repeated tab lists
C-locale byte handling for tabs, backspaces, CR, VT, FF, NUL, and a high byte
Continuous columns and pending blanks across empty files, unterminated files, and stdin operands
Failure for a missing operand while continuing to process a later readable file
Invalid tab width status and diagnostic presence
Empty and unterminated blank input, finite-stop exhaustion and descending-stop rejection.
exclusions: Bash help wording and builtin availability are checked as a contract rather than compared with GNU output.
Write-error recovery after a partial output write is deferred because safely inducing EIO requires a reviewed writer/syscall mock; no absolute device path is used.
Non-C locales, help/version wording, and implementation-specific diagnostic text are outside byte parity assertions.

cases.purpose: Check GNU/POSIX default behavior on stdin: convert only an initial blank run on each line and preserve internal blank runs.
cases.script:
printf '        alpha   beta
  next	value
x        tail
' | unexpand

cases.purpose: Check that -a converts internal runs and --first-only overrides it regardless of option order.
cases.script:
printf '1234567  X        Y
        Z
' | unexpand -a
printf '1234567  X        Y
        Z
' | unexpand -a --first-only
printf '1234567  X        Y
        Z
' | unexpand --first-only -a

cases.purpose: Compare explicit stops, a single repeating width, /N origin-aligned extension, +N extension from the last explicit stop, and repeated -t accumulation on one relative file.
cases.script:
printf '   A    B     C        D\n0123456789  123456789012345\n' > tabs.dat
unexpand -t 4 tabs.dat
unexpand -t '3,7,12' tabs.dat
unexpand -t '3,7,/8' tabs.dat
unexpand -t '3,7,+8' tabs.dat
unexpand -t '3,7' -t '12,+8' tabs.dat

cases.purpose: Check byte-oriented all-blank conversion around backspace, CR, VT, FF, NUL, and byte 0xff under the documented C-locale scope.
cases.script:
printf '1234567  X  	Y
A        Z
x       v\v       w        q
\000       \377  end
' | unexpand -a

cases.purpose: Check that columns and pending blanks continue across unterminated and empty relative files and across a '-' stdin operand.
cases.script:
printf '  ' > prefix.dat
: > empty.dat
printf '      X\n' > suffix.dat
unexpand prefix.dat empty.dat suffix.dat
printf '  ' | unexpand prefix.dat - empty.dat suffix.dat

cases.purpose: Check that -- permits a relative operand whose filename begins with a dash.
Check nonzero status and a diagnostic for a missing relative operand while still emitting the later readable file's converted contents.
cases.script:
printf '        usable\n' > present.dat
if unexpand absent.dat present.dat; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
exit "$status"

cases.purpose: Reject zero tab size with GNU status 1 and a diagnostic.
cases.script:
if unexpand -t 0; then status=0; else status=$?; fi
exit "$status"

cases.purpose: Check the documented Bash integration metadata: unexpand is a builtin and its help entry is available. This is not GNU operation parity.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t unexpand) == builtin ]]
help_text=$(help unexpand)
printf 'builtin\nhelp available\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise the documented output-write failure and early-stop behavior.
Flush a trailing blank run without a newline.
Blanks beyond the final finite tab stop remain literal.
